module_title: Mauryan Empire - Founder, Major Rulers, and the Kalinga War
introduction: The Mauryan Empire was the first large and well-organized empire of ancient India, which strengthened political unity. Its major rulers brought significant changes in administration, warfare, and religion. At this level, we will understand the founder, key rulers, and the Kalinga War in a simple way.

core_concepts.title: Foundation by Chandragupta Maurya
core_concepts.description: Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of Chanakya, defeated the Nanda dynasty in 322 BCE and established the Mauryan Empire. He also defeated the Greek ruler Seleucus Nicator in the northwest.

core_concepts.title: Expansion under Bindusara
core_concepts.description: Bindusara, known as Amitraghata, expanded the empire towards South India and consolidated various regions under his rule.

core_concepts.title: Early Life and Rule of Ashoka
core_concepts.description: Ashoka was a powerful and conquering ruler who initially fought many wars to expand the empire.

core_concepts.title: Impact of the Kalinga War
core_concepts.description: The Kalinga War fought in 261 BCE resulted in massive loss of life, which led to Ashoka’s transformation. He renounced violence and adopted the policy of Dhamma.

core_concepts.title: Extent of the Mauryan Empire
core_concepts.description: The empire extended from Afghanistan to Bengal and from the Himalayas to large parts of South India, making it the largest empire of its time.

important_entities.name: Chandragupta Maurya
important_entities.significance: Ended the Nanda dynasty and laid the foundation of centralized rule

important_entities.name: Bindusara
important_entities.significance: Expanded the empire towards South India

important_entities.name: Ashoka
important_entities.significance: Adopted Buddhism and promoted Dhamma after the Kalinga War

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In most inscriptions, Ashoka is referred to as 'Devanampiya Piyadassi' rather than his actual name. Only a few inscriptions mention the name 'Ashoka'.
It is incorrect to consider Bindusara as a Buddhist; he was a follower of the Ajivika sect.
Students often remember only the war, but its main importance lies in Ashoka’s moral transformation and adoption of Dhamma.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: An easy way to remember the sequence: Chandragupta, Bindusara, and Ashoka.
This trick highlights that Ashoka adopted Buddhism after the Kalinga War.
Helps remember the titles of Bindusara and Ashoka.

exam_strategy_tips: If the term 'Devanampiya Piyadassi' appears, link it to Ashoka.
In questions related to the Kalinga War, always focus on its impact, i.e., the adoption of Dhamma.
